title: A scalar order parameter yields a Cartan one-form, but the direct composite is pure gauge

claim.statement: For an SO(2,3) order parameter g(x), the composite A=g^{-1}dg supplies Lorentz-connection and vierbein components but has identically zero Cartan curvature by the Maurer-Cartan equation.
claim.implication: Form-degree transmutation is possible kinematically, yet independent gravitational dynamics requires an additional adjoint one-form sector or a nontrivial construction beyond the exact Maurer-Cartan form.

interpretation: The coset part of A behaves as a vierbein and the stabilizer part as a spin connection.
Even in a noncommuting chart with nonzero derivative and bracket pieces, Maurer-Cartan cancellation makes the full connection flat.
This realizes relational geometry but not independent gravitational waves.
The minimal escape is A=g^{-1}dg+K, for which F=D_(g^{-1}dg)K+K wedge K; K must have its own transformation law and action.
falsifiers: A nonzero curvature for a smooth exact Maurer-Cartan form would contradict the group identity; the explicit residual is zero.
Global topology, singular defects, or patching can give nontrivial holonomy despite local flatness and are not excluded.
Composite connections involving additional fields or nonlocal operations are not ruled out.
nextBranches: Give K a Yang-Mills/MacDowell-Mansouri-type quadratic action and count its linearized modes.
Test whether candidate-48 descendants can act as a symmetry-breaking compensator selecting the Lorentz subgroup in such an action.
Explore defect or holonomy sectors where a locally flat composite connection has global observables.
